tasks.short: Wear a costume or carry a sign while walking in public to promote an offering.

steps.what: Read the shift assignment, approved message, route and site restrictions.
Collect and fit the costume or sign; check visibility, comfort and safe movement.
Walk the assigned area, display the message and adjust to pedestrians and conditions.

tasks.design: Configure a shift card in the {WORKFLOW} using approved campaign fields and material links from the {DOCS}. The promoter reviews the card before collecting the kit; costume preparation and public promotion remain physical work.
tasks.previous_blocker: The task is mainly physical presence. Small briefing savings rarely justified a separate build.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing forms and templates can assemble the card. AI-assisted coding can reduce the effort of connecting scattered briefing fields.
tasks.still_hard: Costume fit, heat, crowds, accessibility and changing site conditions require attention on location. Software cannot supply the intended human presence.
tasks.human_edge: The promoter brings humour, approachability and awareness of when to engage, give space or stop.
tasks.altitude: The week changes little: the assumed shares imply about 2% less task time. Briefing becomes easier to check, with no additional decision rights.

reach.role: first-line supervisor of retail sales workers
reach.learn: Learn cover planning, site restrictions and practical shift handovers.

evidence.claim: Physical promotion and situational audience engagement largely remain human work.
Configured forms and templates can assemble a briefing from approved structured fields without a model.
The digest provides no direct product evidence or documented case for automating costume or sign-board promotion.

assumptions: The promoter receives an approved campaign brief and shift assignment before public activity.
The time shares are planning estimates, consistent with the strongly physical task prior.
The card assembles existing instructions; it does not invent routes or promotional claims.
The scope excludes audience data collection, location tracking and employee scoring.
Access estimates include checking whether employee consultation applies under national rules; consultation could extend elapsed time.
unknowns: Where campaign briefs and shift assignments are currently held.
Whether the existing brief already serves as a usable shift card.
Whether the employer has a suitable configured form and mobile access.
Which site permissions, breaks and costume restrictions apply.
Whether national rules or employee agreements require consultation for the proposed deployment.
research_questions: Does briefing fragmentation cause enough repeated work to justify configuration?
Can the shift card remain readable and available at the promotion location?
new_work: Maintain approved campaign fields and material links.
Check card updates when routes, shifts or site restrictions change.
Resolve missing assignments and mobile access failures.

role.altitude: The role remains centred on public presence and engagement. Clearer preparation creates modest savings and no automatic expansion of authority.
reach: Support promotional shift planning with a retail supervisor.
role.ambitious_version: A promoter who helps improve campaign briefs and shift arrangements using practical observations from the location.
